title: Shipping a hotfix
subtitle: A small worked example you can edit
description: A deliberately small document, here so you can press Build and watch the loop close before you write your own. Edit any title, press Build again, and the page redraws.

workflows.title: Ship a hotfix
workflows.description: A bug is live and someone has to fix it now. This is the shortest path from report to deployed, and the two ways it usually goes wrong.

summary.trigger: A bug is reported against production
summary.outcome: The fix is live and the reporter has been told

detail.purpose: A fix for a bug you have not seen is a guess. Reproducing first is what separates a hotfix from a second incident.
procedure: Work from the reporter's exact steps before improvising.
Check the deployed version, not `main` — the bug may already be fixed.
If it only reproduces for one account, the cause is data, not code.

failureModes.then: Ask the reporter for a screen recording rather than guessing

steps.title: Is the fix small and obvious?
Mitigate instead of fixing
steps.note: Flag off, roll back, or rate limit

detail.purpose: A big change under time pressure is how a bug becomes an outage. Buy time first, then fix it properly in the normal flow.
procedure: Turn the feature off if there is a flag.
Roll back to the last known good release if there is not.
Say in the incident channel which one you did.

detail.purpose: The only decision that matters here. A hotfix is a promise that the change is too small to go wrong; if it is not, do not make the promise.
rules: One file and no migration is small. Anything touching stored data is not.
If you are unsure, it is not small.

steps.title: Write the failing test first
steps.note: It should fail for the reported reason

detail.purpose: The test is the proof the bug existed and the guard that it stays fixed. Written after the fix, it usually only proves the fix runs.
procedure: Assert the behaviour the reporter expected, not the code path you plan to change.
Run it and watch it fail before touching the fix.

steps.title: Make the smallest change that passes

detail.purpose: Every extra line in a hotfix is unreviewed risk shipped at speed. Tidying is a separate pull request on a normal day.
rules: If the diff is over about thirty lines, go back and reconsider the scope question.
Leave the TODO. Someone will thank you for the small diff.

detail.purpose: A green new test and a red suite means the fix traded one bug for another. The suite is the only signal that matters before deploy.

commands.note: Full run, not the filtered one you used while working

steps.title: Deploy and watch it
steps.note: Stay until the error rate settles

detail.purpose: Deploying is not the end of the job. The five minutes after are when you find out whether you were right.
procedure: Watch the error rate for the affected endpoint, not the global one.
Have the rollback command in your terminal before you deploy, not after.

steps.title: Tell the person who reported it
steps.note: In the place they reported it

detail.purpose: The bug is not closed until the person who found it knows. This is the step that gets skipped, and it is the one they remember.
procedure: Reply where they reported it, not in a ticket they cannot see.
Say what was wrong in one sentence and what you changed in one more.
